body:
AUDIO/PRIVACY LEAD: Browser microphone permission is not legal consent. Default hardware/data boundary is presenter-only directional/headset mic; do not capture the room/audience. Audience questions are paused by default or use a dedicated consent-noticed mic. Before `getUserMedia`, Console shows a separate, unbundled capture notice naming controller, purposes (live STT/RAG), vendors/region, recipients, data retained, exact retention, withdrawal/deletion path, and policy version. For consent-based processing it requires affirmative opt-in; other lawful bases require counsel-configured policy + notice. Record only `{session, subject, policy_version/hash, purposes, timestamp, locale}`, never speech as proof. Audience origin has `Permissions-Policy: microphone=()`; only top-level Console can request it.

Server enforcement: audio frames are accepted only with a short-lived `CaptureGrant(session, capture_device, subject, purpose, policy_version, expiry)` issued after acknowledgment. One capture device at a time. Persistent red REC + timer + one-click STOP; any authorized presenter device can stop. Stop/session end/logout/revocation/control-channel loss invokes `MediaStreamTrack.stop()` for every track, clears `srcObject`, closes uploader/vendor stream, revokes grant and zeroes buffers. Browser UI is not the enforcement boundary—the ingest service drops every frame after revocation.

Data-minimizing default: raw PCM is memory-only with <=30s rolling retry buffer and is never written to disk/object storage/logs. Final transcript is private, encrypted and used only for live coaching/report materialization; attach `delete_after` at creation (recommended: delete immediately after successful report, hard cap 24h after session end). Derived reports remain personal data and follow the same user/tenant deletion unless user explicitly elects retention. No raw queries/transcripts in telemetry, crash reports or vendor dashboards. STT/LLM contract must prohibit training/human review, bound provider retention, expose deletion, region and subprocessors.

Deletion must be a tested cascade keyed by session/data-subject: stop ingest -> buffers/queues -> STT provider job -> transcript/object DB -> embeddings/vector index -> prompt/cache -> report/export/analytics. Idempotent deletion outbox records only object IDs/status, not content; each store must acknowledge. Encrypt per session so DEK destruction gives immediate crypto-erasure; backup copies expire within a disclosed maximum (recommend <=30d) and deletion tombstones reapply on restore. Legal hold is explicit, narrowly ACL'd, reasoned + expiring and UI says `retained under hold`, never falsely `deleted`.

Acceptance tests: no grant/no consent audio rejected; audience origin mic denied; revoke midstream drops next frame; raw audio absent from durable stores/logs; session end closes vendor job; deletion removes transcript/embedding/cache/report and survives backup restore; provider failure leaves deletion pending + alerts, never success.

Legal baseline (confirm per deployment): GDPR Arts 5/7/17/25/28/32 and Korea PIPA Arts 15/16/21/29 support lawful purpose, minimization, storage limitation/destruction and safeguards; erasure is not absolute. Sources: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj/eng ; https://www.law.go.kr/%EB%B2%95%EB%A0%B9/%EA%B0%9C%EC%9D%B8%EC%A0%95%EB%B3%B4%EB%B3%B4%ED%98%B8%EB%B2%95 ; https://www.pipc.go.kr/eng/user/lgp/law/lawsRegulations.do ; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/uk-gdpr-guidance-and-resources/lawful-basis/consent/what-is-valid-consent/ ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getUserMedia#privacy_and_security ; https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaStreamTrack/stop
